title: Developer Discovery Lab: SDK & Quickstart Initiative
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Run a focused initiative to reduce first-time integration time for engineers using Redwood Inference SDKs and quickstarts. 'Developer Discovery Lab' bundles a set of language SDKs, three interactive quickstarts, and a micro-telemetry pipeline to measure time-to-first-success. The initiative prioritizes Python and Typescript SDK parity, one-click quickstarts for hosted API and Dedicated, and a canonical set of evaluation prompts for onboarding regressions.

Scope:
- Complete SDK parity surface (Python, Typescript, Go minimal) for auth, streaming, and function-calling flows.
- Ship 3 quickstarts: Chat app (TS), Batch embeddings pipeline (Python), and On-prem smoke test (Go).
- Add SDK integration tests to CI and a small telemetry hook to capture onboarding funnels (opt-in).
- Docs: concise quickstart pages, runnable samples, and troubleshooting matrix.

Goals / OKRs (measurable):
- O1: Decrease median time-to-first-success (TTFS) from sign-up to a successful API call in quickstart sample by 40% within 8 weeks. Metric tracked via onboarding telemetry dashboard.
- O2: Increase SDK adoption signal: 25% growth in SDK downloads (pypi/npm) quarter-over-quarter for the prioritized languages.
- O3: Zero critical regressions: shipping SDK unit tests + CI coverage leads to <=1 critical regression post-release.

Success Criteria:
- Quickstarts show end-to-end completion in <15 minutes for a new user (measured via funnel).
- SDKs pass language-specific compatibility tests against runtime-1.20 in CI.
- Docs reach >75% task completion rate in usability checks with external engineers.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full enterprise-ready Go SDK feature parity (only minimal onboarding bits).
- Large-scale telemetry analytics (we will emit events to an internal topic; processing pipeline tracked as follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- All three quickstarts published with runnable code examples and a short video walkthrough link.
- SDKs released to package registries with semantic-versioned tags and CHANGELOG entries.
- Automated CI checks for quickstart smoke tests and SDK unit tests passing on main.
- Onboarding funnel instrumentation emits the agreed event schema and is visible in the debug dashboard.
- Docs reviewed and approved by Content and Design (sign-off recorded in comments).

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: SDK refactor touches streaming/function-calling surfaces and may cause regressions. Mitigation: create focused test harnesses, gate changes behind feature flags, and run canary SDK releases to a small set of internal teams (ENG pilot).
Risk: Telemetry opt-in complexity may slow adoption. Mitigation: keep opt-in default for internal builds, provide clear privacy text and a minimal event schema.
Risk: Docs may not be discoverable. Mitigation: update Console onboarding route to surface quickstarts and add a short checklist in user welcome emails.

implementation_notes:
- Keep SDK surface small and idiomatic per-language; avoid introducing cross-language API baggage.
- Telemetry events limited to: quickstart_started, quickstart_completed, sample_api_call_success, sample_api_call_error. Event schema in docs folder.
- Use environment variable REDWOOD_DEV_DISCOVERY to toggle extra debug output in SDKs for testers.
- Follow release cadence: canary -> internal-beta -> public patch.
